overview.short: Bhimeswar Dham, is a Hindu temple, located at Dakini hill (also known as Daini pahar) near Pamohi in Guwahati, Assam, India.
overview.description: Bhimeswar Dham, is a Hindu temple, located at Dakini hill (also known as Daini pahar) near Pamohi in Guwahati, Assam, India. It is situated at the hill just besides the Deepor Beel. It is believed that Shiva had incarnated here to destroy a demon called Bhimasura and protect his devotees. The exact location of Dakini is a debated subject.

topPlaces.name: Betkuchi
topPlaces.description: Betkuchi is a verdant locality on the southwestern outskirts of Guwahati near Pamohi, surrounded by rolling hills, tea gardens, and forested streams of Kamrup Metropolitan district.

image.alt: Aerial view of lush green tea gardens and forest in Kamrup near Betkuchi

topPlaces.name: Garchuk Lachit Garh
topPlaces.description: Garchuk Lachit Garh is a historical earthen fortification and rampart constructed during the medieval Ahom kingdom under General Lachit Borphukan to defend Guwahati.

image.alt: Monument of General Lachit Borphukan overlooking the Brahmaputra banks in Assam

topPlaces.name: Swahid Smarak Kshetra
topPlaces.description: Swahid Smarak Kshetra is a landscaped memorial park and garden in Paschim Boragaon, Guwahati, built to honor the martyrs of the Assam Movement amidst green manicured grounds.

image.alt: Scenic landscaped memorial park featuring serene water and manicured greenery

topPlaces.name: Jyotikuchi
topPlaces.description: Jyotikuchi is a scenic residential foothill neighborhood in southwest Guwahati bordering the Pamohi river valley and green hillsides of the Southern Kamrup range.

image.alt: Peaceful evening over a calm lake with stunning twilight colors reflecting across the horizon

topPlaces.name: Borjhar (LGBI Airport)
topPlaces.description: Borjhar is the premier aviation and transport gateway of Northeast India, home to the Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport surrounded by scenic paddy fields and hills.

image.alt: Captivating view of an airplane on the runway during a golden sunset at Borjhar airport gateway

topPlaces.name: Dhirenpara
topPlaces.description: Dhirenpara is a vibrant valley neighborhood in south Guwahati situated close to the Pamohi hills, offering quick access to the peaceful forested tracks of Bhimeswar Dham.

image.alt: Tall areca palm trees and lush green tropical foliage in an open grove in Kamrup, Assam

topPlaces.name: Dipor Bil
topPlaces.description: Dipor Bil (Deepor Beel) is a designated Ramsar wetland and perennial freshwater lake in southwest Guwahati, renowned for water lilies, migratory aquatic birds, and scenic sunset reflections.

image.alt: Authentic scenic panorama of Dipor Bil lake waters stretching toward the foothills in southwest Guwahati

topPlaces.name: Deepar Beel Wildlife Sanctuary
topPlaces.description: Deepar Beel Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected wetland sanctuary adjacent to Bhimeswar Dham, serving as a critical refuge for over 200 bird species including greater adjutant storks and migratory waterfowl.

image.alt: Painted storks peacefully wading and feeding in the shallow wetland waters of Deepar Beel Wildlife Sanctuary

items.note: Betkuchi is the locality in Guwahati, Assam, India; surrounded by the localities of Jyotikuchi, Lokhra and Garchuk.

Garchuk Lachit Garh (meaning 'fort' in Assamese) or Fort, now popularly known as Lachit Garh, is located in northeastern India in the southwestern part of Guwahati city to the west of Ahomgaon. The fort was constructed under the Ahom kingdom during the times of Lachit Borphukan around the year 1669-70 CE, and stretches from the northern Fatasil hills at Garchuk locality cutting across the National Highway (N.H.)-37 at Garchuk Charali to the southern hills via Pamahi and Moinakhurung.

Swahid Smarak Kshetra is a memorial and park in Boragaon, Guwahati, Assam, India, dedicated to the martyrs of the historic Assam Movement (1979–1985). The memorial commemorates the sacrifice of 860 numbers of agitators who lost their lives during the mass movement that sought to protect the cultural, linguistic and territorial identity of Assam.
Jyotikuchi is a locality in Guwahati. It is surrounded by the localities of Lokhra, Sawkuchi and Barsapara.

Borjhar is a locality in Guwahati, situated on the western fringes of the metropolitan expanse of the city. Jalukbari is 12 km to the east with nearest Railway station and junction at Azara and Kamakhya respectively.
Dhirenpara is a locality of Guwahati. It is situated in the eastern side of a beautiful high mountain.

Dipor Bil, also spelled Deepor Beel (Pron: dɪpɔ:(r) bɪl) (bil or beel means "lake" in the local Assamese language), is located to the south-west of Guwahati city, in Kamrup Metropolitan district of Assam, India. It is a permanent freshwater lake, in a former channel of the Brahmaputra River, to the south of the main river.
Deepar Beel Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area in Assam, India. It is located to the south-west of Guwahati, covering an area of about 4.14 km².

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Bhimeswar Dham?
faq.a: The best time to visit Bhimeswar Dham is Oct – Mar. Summers are 25–42°C and winters are 7–24°C.

faq.q: How do I reach Bhimeswar Dham?
faq.a: The nearest airport is Bhimeswar Dham / nearest airport (30 km) and the nearest railway station is Guwahati Railway Station (11 km). Roads are generally good; check seasonal/monsoon conditions before high-altitude or remote stretches.

faq.q: How many days are enough for Bhimeswar Dham?
faq.a: 3 days are usually enough to cover the top attractions of Bhimeswar Dham at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: How much does a hotel cost in Bhimeswar Dham?
